prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1471; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both drivers reported no visible damage to the front of the insured's vehicle beyond minor bumper scuffing. Photos of both vehicles obtained from the insured.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Attorney letter of representation received requesting that all communications be directed to counsel's office. Claimant reports neck and back strain and has been advised to seek medical evaluation. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel for signature. Reserve set for bodily injury and property damage pending records.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of medical records. Counsel indicates the claimant attended an urgent care visit and is scheduled for follow-up with a primary care physician and physical therapy. Requested itemized bills and treatment notes. Counsel stated the claimant is still experiencing stiffness and limited range of motion in the neck and lower back.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed by appraiser. Rear bumper cover, trunk lid and tail light assembly on the claimant's vehicle identified as damaged. Repair estimate received and reviewed. Supplemental photos uploaded to file. Rental coverage confirmed for the claimant's vehicle during repair period per policy terms.

Entry 5: Received updated medical records and billing from claimant's counsel. Diagnosis consistent with cervical and lumbar strain. Treatment plan includes physical therapy and periodic reassessment. Liability assessed as clear in favor of the insured. File referred to supervisor for review of bodily injury evaluation. Counsel advised that further correspondence will follow once the review is complete.
